atelier_description: Start with routing, typed API queries and authentication already wired together. Add your own modules while lint rules and architecture tests check the boundaries.
atelier_hero_note: MIT-licensed and currently in alpha. Read the source before you choose.
atelier_built_with: The stack you will work with
atelier_layer_page_desc: Normalize route parameters and choose a screen. Reusable workflows belong in the feature module.
atelier_layer_feature_desc: Keep queries, form behavior and feature rules together. Export what other modules need through the module's public entry point.
atelier_layer_core_desc: Shared infrastructure defines API and permission contracts. Framework-independent code lives in core/lib.
atelier_preview_direction: Routes call features; features use shared infrastructure.
atelier_preview_caption: Select a layer to see what it owns
atelier_foundation_title: The decisions you would otherwise repeat.
atelier_foundation_desc: Routing, permissions, data access and interface components already share the same conventions. Read a reference module to see how they fit together.
atelier_boundaries_desc: Lint flags deep cross-module imports and Vue Query imports in route pages. Architecture tests check module registrations and navigation contracts.
atelier_auth_title: Choose how your backend signs users in
atelier_auth_desc: JWT, OAuth and cookie-session adapters share session restoration and permission-aware routes. Each adapter declares which sign-in features the interface can show.
atelier_toolchain_title: Let the generator prepare the module
atelier_toolchain_desc: Scaffold modules and pages with their registrations. Vite+ runs the formatting, lint, types, tests and builds used in this repository.
atelier_design_eyebrow: A theme changes more than color
atelier_design_title: Try the same screen in twelve styles.
atelier_design_desc: The twelve themes use a shared component layer, with distinct palettes, type choices and shapes. Switch between them here, then customize your project in brand.css.
atelier_design_note: Your selection updates this page. You can also compare dark mode and the Arabic layout.
atelier_specimen_title: See how type changes the interface.
atelier_working_title: Look through a feature before you start.
atelier_customers_desc: Follow a record from paginated list to editable form, including query validation and save errors.
atelier_components_desc: Check the fields, navigation and feedback patterns available to feature screens.
atelier_testing_desc: See how unit, integration and browser tests cover the template, and which checks your own application will need.
atelier_closing_title: Start your own project from the template.
atelier_closing_desc: Take a copy, remove the demo modules and add your first feature. The setup guide explains how to keep receiving template updates.
home_feature_theme_desc: Twelve design personalities share one token vocabulary across light and dark modes.
atelier_workflow_title: Start with a module you can read.
atelier_workflow_desc: Generate a collection module, then replace its placeholder fields with your domain. The module is registered and its permissions declared; you decide which roles receive them.
atelier_workflow_preview_label: Generated module, before your domain edits
atelier_workflow_note: The scaffold includes queries, routes, mock handlers and locale files. Business rules, role grants and translations are still yours to write.
atelier_workflow_step1_desc: Use --dry-run to inspect the generator's file and registry changes before it writes anything.
atelier_workflow_step2_desc: Replace the placeholder fields, then adapt the list, form and mock records to your data.
atelier_workflow_step3_desc: Grant access to the right roles, translate the labels, and configure the API contract for your backend.
atelier_ownership_eyebrow: Taking updates as your project grows
atelier_ownership_title: Know which files an update can change.
atelier_ownership_desc: Vuestrata records file ownership so you can take upstream fixes without treating every file the same. Your modules and customization files stay under your control.
atelier_ownership_managed_desc: UI wrappers and core infrastructure receive upstream updates while untouched. If you edit one, the incoming version is held for review.
atelier_ownership_merged_desc: Framework-owned content can update while entries in your app: regions are kept. Keep the region markers in place.
atelier_ownership_seeded_desc: Branding, auth settings and other customization files are written once. After that, they are yours; upgrades leave them alone.
atelier_ownership_note: Preview an update with vuestrata diff. When a file cannot be applied safely, review its copy in .vuestrata/incoming/ before adopting the result.
atelier_faq_desc: What the template provides, what you configure, and what to expect from the current release.
atelier_faq_backend_q: Does it work with my backend?
atelier_faq_backend_a: The API layer has presets for Laravel, Django, Spring, ASP.NET and NestJS conventions, such as validation errors and CSRF. Laravel, Django and Spring also have pagination dialects. You still configure endpoints and an auth adapter; your backend enforces permissions and business rules.
atelier_faq_license_q: Can I use it in a commercial project?
atelier_faq_license_a: Vuestrata is MIT-licensed. You can use it in a commercial application and modify the source; keep its copyright and license notice. Third-party packages and assets retain their own licenses.
atelier_faq_upgrade_a: Upgrade compares files with the recorded baseline. Untouched managed files can update. Managed files you edited stay in place, with the new version held for review; seeded customization files are left alone. Run vuestrata diff first, then apply and test the changes.
atelier_faq_alpha_a: The current release is in the 1.1 alpha series. You can try the demo and start a project, but conventions and public APIs may change between releases. Read the release notes before upgrading and validate your backend and deployment for your own application.
